system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

[SLICE BEGIN]
# Outcome sub-dossier — Inland American Real Estate Trust: realized record of the Concord Debt Holdings LLC joint venture (fixed ~2012-2014 window)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier reports ONLY the realized record
> after the venture was entered; it contains no information about how the venture was
> structured at inception. The outcome window is fixed at approximately 2012-2014 (three
> to five years after the ~2009 reference period), corresponding to the registrant's
> fiscal-2012 through fiscal-2014 annual reports.

## Realized trajectory of the venture shortly after inception (pre-window, cited transparently)
- The venture deteriorated rapidly: during 2009 Concord received margin calls on certain
  of its loan facilities requiring it to identify loans for disposal to meet pay-down
  requirements, and recorded impairment losses and loan-loss reserves of $225.1 million
  for the year ended December 31, 2009. [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-10-000005, Form 10-K (FY2009) financial-statement notes]
- Inland American's share of the venture's net loss reduced the carrying value of its
  investment to $(9.9) million as of December 31, 2009, recorded "up to the amount at
  which the Company approximately believes it is obligated to fund." [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-10-000005, Form 10-K (FY2009) financial-statement notes]
- On December 22, 2009, Lexington Realty Trust, Winthrop Realty Trust, Inland American,
  and their respective subsidiaries entered into a settlement agreement resolving the IA
  Sub v. Concord action; it provides, among other things, for termination of any party's
  obligation to contribute capital to Concord, equal allocation of distributions among
  Inland, Lexington and Winthrop, and formation of a new entity to be owned by their
  subsidiaries — conditioned on cancellation of certain CDO bonds held by Concord Debt
  Funding Trust by August 14, 2010. [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-10-000005, Form 10-K (FY2009) financial-statement notes]

## Status entering the fixed window
- By the fiscal-2010 annual report (filed 2011), the Concord Debt joint venture is
  referenced only historically — in the year-over-year comparison of prior (2009) losses
  ("significant losses incurred and impairments recorded by our Concord Debt joint
  venture in 2009") — and carries no active current-year carrying value. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-11-064003, Form 10-K (FY2010) MD&A]

## Within the fixed window (fiscal 2012-2014)
- The fiscal-2012 annual report does not separately disclose the Concord Debt Holdings LLC
  joint venture or Lex-Win Concord LLC among the registrant's unconsolidated ventures;
  the specific venture's realized record is therefore not separately disclosed within the
  fixed window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-13-000007, Form 10-K (FY2012)]
- Because the specific venture's outcome is not separately disclosed within the fixed
  2012-2014 window, the venture-specific realized record for that window is coded
  **uncertain (no separate public disclosure within the window)**; it is not inferred.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-13-000007, Form 10-K (FY2012)]
- Entity-level context within the window: the registrant reported a net loss attributable
  to the Company of $(69,338) thousand (approximately $69.3 million) for the year ended
  December 31, 2012 (compared with net losses of $(316,253) thousand for 2011 and
  $(176,431) thousand for 2010). [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-13-000007, Form 10-K (FY2012) consolidated statements of operations]
- The registrant remained named "Inland American Real Estate Trust, Inc." through its
  fiscal-2014 annual report (filed March 27, 2015); the name "InvenTrust Properties" does
  not appear in that filing, indicating any renaming occurred after the fixed window.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-15-000008, Form 10-K (FY2014)]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The venture's realized record concentrated shortly after inception: heavy 2009
  impairments and loan-loss reserves at the venture level ($225.1 million), a reduction of
  the registrant's carrying value to $(9.9) million by December 31, 2009, and a December
  2009 settlement terminating the parties' capital-contribution obligations and forming a
  successor entity. [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-10-000005, Form 10-K (FY2009) financial-statement notes] By the fixed 2012-2014 window the venture is no longer
  separately disclosed (referenced only historically in fiscal 2010, absent from fiscal
  2012), so the venture-specific outcome within the window is uncertain; the registrant
  itself continued to report entity-level net losses (~$69.3 million for fiscal 2012) and
  retained its Inland American name through fiscal 2014. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-11-064003, Form 10-K (FY2010) MD&A] [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-13-000007, Form 10-K (FY2012)] [SRC: SEC accession 0001307748-15-000008, Form 10-K (FY2014)]

[SLICE END]

There is no documented evidence of product/process incoherence (p4) or process/organization fracture (p5) during the outcome window."
}
